items.title: Major US outlets boycott shared Trump coverage in protest at media ban
items.description: Regular coverage of the president has been disrupted after he banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.

items.title: Lithuania ready to 'fight back' but has evacuation plans in face of Russia threats, PM tells BBC
items.description: Sinkevičius told BBC Newsnight Lithuanians feel "constantly threatened" by Moscow, but the nation was prepared to "fight back" if attacked.

items.title: Iran must stop arming Houthis in Yemen, G7 says ahead of UN General Assembly
items.description: The G7 also condemns "in the strongest terms" Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying that the escalation in fighting in Yemen jeopardises global energy security.

items.title: Eleven injured in shooting outside Turkish school
items.description: Footage appears to show a male in the area carrying a firearm, while officials say the attacker has been captured.

items.title: Sri Lankan court to deliver verdict on deadly Easter bombings
items.description: Co-ordinated suicide attacks killed 270 people across several churches and hotels in Colombo in 2019.

items.title: Outrage in India over viral video of teen molested and her friend beaten
items.description: Three minors were arrested after videos capturing the assault went viral in India, sparking anger.

items.title: Doctor in court to face Rwanda genocide charges in UK
items.description: Dr Vincent Brown was charged following a seven year British investigation into the 1994 killings.

items.title: Four dead after powerful Typhoon Dujuan lashes Japan
items.description: The storm pulled away from Japan after bringing heavy rains and strong winds to Tokyo and surrounding areas.

items.title: British man missing after diving into Lake Como to rescue teenager
items.description: The UK Foreign Office says it is supporting the man's family and working with local authorities.

items.title: Texas ICE shooting leaves Venezuelan DoorDash driver with bullet in his back, says lawyer
items.description: The delivery driver was transferred from a hospital to a detention centre, his lawyer tells US media.

items.title: Canadian province sues OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge school shooting
items.description: British Columbia has accused the company of failing to report the shooter's troubling interactions with ChatGPT to law enforcement.

items.title: Infantino says he is open to talks over Fifa reform
items.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates. shifting tone as he seeks support to stay on.

items.title: To Kill A Mockingbird first edition found in London charity shop
items.description: An original US edition of To Kill a Mockingbird is found in an Oxfam store in west London.

items.title: Merz vows to keep coalition together for Germany's 'democratic future'
items.description: The chancellor has come under increasing pressure after resounding state election defeats, but says the results "go far beyond my own person"

items.title: Russia's elections had few surprises - but how the Kremlin uses the results will be crucial
items.description: Vladimir Putin will likely use the result to claim most Russians back the so-called special military operation in Ukraine, writes the BBC's Steve Rosenberg.

items.title: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups form new alliance
items.description: The groups have been active in Ethiopia's most populous regions for years and now say they will work together.

items.title: US strikes on alleged drug boats could be crimes against humanity, says UN
items.description: A report says the attacks, of which there have been at least 68, were not self-defence.

items.title: Two charged with woman's murder as South Africa police investigate eight other body finds
items.description: The body of Jabulile Ntimba was the ninth to be found recently in an area east of Johannesburg.

items.title: Why a Bollywood celebrity manager's 2020 death case has been reopened
items.description: Disha Salian's father insists her death was not suicide or an accident, but that she was gang-raped and murdered.

items.title: Merz's political crisis threatens Germany's obsession with stability
items.description: Political shifts in Germany are being watched closely in Europe and beyond, Katya Adler writes.
